title: Go SDK: typed adapters and streaming combinators
creator: Alyssa Moreno
description: Add a set of ergonomic, type-safe adapters to the Go SDK that make decoding structured outputs from streaming responses straightforward, and provide combinators for composing partial JSON frames into typed Go structs. Deliverables include a small codec/generic helper layer, streaming combinators that preserve backpressure and cancellations, and a retry shim that composes with stream decoding so resume/retry semantics are correct for idempotent requests.
acceptance_criteria: Provide DecodeStreamTo[T](ctx, stream, &T) helper that maps streaming events to typed struct T with clear error semantics
Provide StreamCombiner utilities to merge partial JSON tokens/chunks into valid JSON documents for DecodeStreamTo[T] without buffering entire responses
Expose retry middleware (RetryShim) that can safely replay idempotent requests and resumes stream decoding when feasible
Include examples in sdk/go/examples/typed_streaming showing chat + structured tool-call decoding and token-level cancellation
Unit tests covering: malformed partial JSON, mid-stream retry, context cancellation, and backpressure under high concurrency
Benchmark demonstrating <=5% latency overhead vs raw stream consumption for typical chat->struct workloads
discussion: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting. Agreed goal: make decoding ergonomic for app developers who expect typed responses (structs) from streaming endpoints without forcing them to load full responses into memory.

2026-03-02: Design trade-off: two approaches considered: (A) passive token accumulator that reconstructs JSON fragments, (B) incremental decoder using json.Decoder with io.Reader adapter. We chose a hybrid: small non-blocking buffer plus incremental decoding to handle partial chunks and preserve streaming semantics.
2026-03-04: Decided generics-based API surface: DecodeStreamTo[T], StreamMapper[T], and StreamCombiner. This keeps callsites concise and avoids reflection-heavy code paths.

2026-03-06: Retry semantics debate: naive retry would double-apply side-effects. Agreed to require caller-provided idempotency token or request-level idempotency flag. RetryShim will be opt-in and will only replay when configured and when server-side resume tokens are provided in the protocol.

2026-03-09: UX review by Lina Gomez (PM) and Tomoko Saito (Design) — asked for explicit examples showing error messages for partial-decoding failures and recommended adding a small troubleshooting page with common failure modes.
2026-03-10: Engineering review completed. PR opened and assigned for code review. Performance microbenchmarks added to CI.
implementation_notes: API proposals: DecodeStreamTo[T](ctx context.Context, src StreamReader, out *T) error and StreamCombiner that implements io.Reader over token chunks
Implement small ring buffer (<=8KB) used to accumulate incomplete tokens to avoid large allocations for well-formed streams
Use encoding/json.Decoder with custom io.Reader that yields chunks from StreamReader to decode objects incrementally
Expose StreamMapper[T](fn func(T) error) to handle per-object callbacks without copying into slices
RetryShim: middleware that records client-side idempotency token and coordinates with runtime resume tokens. Only replays when server indicates replay-safe or when request explicitly idempotent
Add tests: mocked stream with chunk boundary at arbitrary positions, test cancellations, test partial JSON escape sequences
Benchmarks: compare decode latency and allocations against baseline using bytes.Buffer + json.Unmarshal on full payload
risks: Edge cases in incremental JSON tokenization could cause subtle decode errors for streaming models that emit non-JSON noise between messages
Retry semantics rely on server-side resume tokens; without them, Replay could lead to duplicate side effects if caller misconfigures idempotency
Generics usage complicates go1.17 compatibility; we will gate on go1.20+, update SDK minimum if required
Performance overhead for tiny responses must be minimal; need microbenchmarks across realistic traffic patterns
dependencies: ENG-51111 - runtime: add resume token support to streaming protocol
ENG-51722 - sdk-go: upgrade minimum Go to 1.20
PM-298 - docs: add troubleshooting page for streaming decoders
